name: Chromatic punch word

source.description: An inspected kinetic-type piece (batch 1, 2026-11-26) lands each single word on the beat with an oversized entrance and a red/cyan channel split that settles in a few frames.

technique: A single word enters about 20% oversized with red and cyan copies offset sideways, and in 2-4 frames scales to size while the copies collapse into one clean word. The split reads as impact and speed without a camera shake.
purpose: Give one-word beats weight in a fast, music-led sequence.
visual_behaviour: Frame 1: word large, fringed red on one side and cyan on the other; frames 2-4: fringes close and size settles; then the word holds clean.
mechanics: Three stacked copies (or text-shadow): red at -dx, cyan at +dx, white on top with mix-blend-mode screen on dark; dx 8-14 px -> 0 and scale 1.2 -> 1.0 over 0.10-0.15 s with power4.out, placed on the beat. Optional 1-frame opacity flicker on the fringes.

decomposition.timing: Settle 0.10-0.15 s; one word per beat (0.5-1.0 s).

use_cases: stat or claim slams in a promo
hook lines in a short-form film
failure_modes: Red/cyan fringes on a light canvas look like misregistration; use on dark sections or swap to the accent pair
A split that never settles hurts legibility
Every word punched equally flattens the hierarchy; punch only the beat words

implementation.approach: text-shadow: calc(var(--dx) * -1) 0 #ff2a4a, var(--dx) 0 #2ad4ff; tween --dx and scale with fromTo(immediateRender) on the beat from Studio.rhythm.grid; deterministic.

provenance.observed: Each new word ('DETOURS', 'MILLION', 'YOU BLINKED.') enters about 120% oversized with red and cyan copies offset sideways and settles to one clean word within about 2-3 frames.
The opening statement lands with red-cyan split copies (1.55 s) and the next word swaps in with a one-frame split (2.05 s).
